cards.name: Farm
cards.flavor: Where the river runs close, the first farmers sow wheat and barley, and learn what all farming teaches: how to wait.

cards.name: Palisade
cards.flavor: Sharpened logs and a ditch around the village. On moonless nights it is enough, because everyone agrees that it is.

cards.name: Settler
cards.flavor: Families load their oxcarts with seed grain and walk until they find good water and land no one has claimed. Then they stay.

cards.name: Scout
cards.flavor: A runner goes ahead of the tribe, reading the land for rivers, passes, and the thin smoke of other people's fires.

cards.name: Barter
cards.flavor: Obsidian for salt, wool for copper. At the river ford both sides walk away richer, each certain the other was a fool.

cards.name: Hunt
cards.flavor: The herds move through the long grass like weather, and the hunters follow, as their parents did, and bring meat home at dusk.

cards.name: Net Fishing
cards.flavor: At dawn two boats draw a net between them across the shallows and haul it in together, silver and thrashing.

cards.name: Bread and Beer
cards.flavor: Grain feeds the city twice, as bread and as beer: the daily ration of every worker in Sumer and Egypt.

cards.name: Land Grants
cards.flavor: The ruler parcels out fields to loyal soldiers, and villages take root along the boundary stones, full of old campaigns.

cards.name: Feast
cards.flavor: Oxen are roasted, jars are opened, and for one night the whole city eats together. In the morning the grievances are still there.

cards.name: Runner
cards.flavor: Runners cross the plain from town to town by nightfall, carrying the message word for word in their heads.

cards.name: Tribute
cards.flavor: Each spring the outlying towns send jars of oil, bolts of cloth and silver rings, and a little less than they promised.

cards.name: Assembly of Elders
cards.flavor: In the early cities of Sumer an assembly of elders meets at the gate, hears every grievance and decides by slow agreement.

cards.name: Slash and Burn
cards.flavor: Fire runs through the brush and the ash feeds the soil. In three years the field is spent and the farmers move on.

cards.name: Corvée
cards.flavor: Every household owes the ruler a season of labour: digging canals, hauling stone, raising walls they will never live behind.

cards.name: Storyteller
cards.flavor: By the fire the old tales are told again, the floods, the heroes, the gods, and each generation learns what the last one feared.

cards.name: Research
cards.flavor: Priests watch the stars and scribes copy tables, and slowly the temple archives fill with everything anyone has learned.

cards.name: Forage
cards.flavor: When the stores run thin, the young go out at dawn and come back with roots, nuts, and the odd unlucky hare.

cards.name: Caravan
cards.flavor: Strings of donkeys, later camels, sway from city to city across desert and steppe, carrying tin, cloth and news.

cards.name: Sea Trade
cards.flavor: A ship works its way along the coast from port to port, trading cedar for copper and oil for wine, and comes home riding low.

cards.name: Precedent
cards.flavor: Scribes keep the verdicts on clay. When a case comes before the judges, they read how the last one like it was settled.

cards.name: Read the Stars
cards.flavor: Night after night the astronomers of Babylon chart the planets from the temple roof and write down what each sign foretells.

cards.name: Temple
cards.flavor: A house for the god on a raised platform. The priests keep the offerings, and the people climb the steps with their hopes.

cards.name: Great Temple
cards.flavor: Its courts hold workshops, granaries, scribes and a god, and half the city's land answers to it, though seldom to the god.

cards.name: Monument
cards.flavor: A carved stone in the square tells every passer-by of the ruler's victories. Within a generation, no one stops to read it.

cards.name: Pyramids
cards.flavor: At Giza, work gangs called Friends of Khufu haul two million blocks into place, so that one king might climb to the stars.

cards.name: Oracle of Delphi
cards.flavor: Above the sacred spring at Delphi the Pythia speaks for Apollo, and kings travel far to hear answers that fit any question.

cards.name: Walls of Uruk
cards.flavor: Gilgamesh, the poem says, raised Uruk's walls, nine kilometres of kiln-fired brick: a boast against death, still partly standing.

cards.name: Great Ziggurat
cards.flavor: At Ur a stepped mountain of brick lifts the moon god's shrine high above the plain and the flood, a little nearer the moon.

cards.name: Hanging Gardens
cards.flavor: In Babylon, they say, terraces of trees climb toward the sky, watered by machines that lift the river. No one you ask has seen them.

cards.name: Great Library
cards.flavor: Alexandria's library means to hold every book in the world. It copies the scrolls off every ship that docks, and keeps the originals.

cards.name: Great Harbor of Tyre
cards.flavor: Tyre's island keeps two harbours, one facing Sidon and one facing Egypt, and the trade of the whole sea comes to them by name.

cards.name: Lighthouse of Pharos
cards.flavor: On Pharos island a tower of white stone keeps a fire burning all night, and ships see Alexandria long before the coast.

cards.name: Royal Road
cards.flavor: From Sardis to Susa runs the Persian king's road, and at every station a fresh horse and rider wait for news they may not read.

cards.name: Pasture
cards.flavor: The herders follow their flocks across the open grass and count them every dusk, and the counting is a kind of prayer.

cards.name: Harbor
cards.flavor: Stone quays and a breakwater make a port of the bay, where ships ride out the storms and sailors learn the word for home.

cards.name: Hunters' Camp
cards.flavor: At the forest edge the hunters dry meat and stretch hides by the fire, and do not speak of what they saw among the trees.

cards.name: Timber Camp
cards.flavor: Axes ring all day in the forest, and the logs go downriver to become beams, hulls and charcoal: a city, and then its smoke.

cards.name: Irrigation Canals
cards.flavor: The canals carry the river across the fields; the silt fills them in; every spring the digging begins again, as it always will.

cards.name: Ploughed Fields
cards.flavor: Oxen lean into the yoke where people once broke the soil by hand, and one family now feeds many it will never meet.

cards.name: Weavers' Workshop
cards.flavor: Spindles whirl and looms clack as wool and flax become cloth, the first great trade of the cities, made one thread at a time.

cards.name: Brewery
cards.flavor: Barley mash foams in the great jars. Beer is food, wage and offering, and the brewers are never idle, nor ever quite sober.

cards.name: Olive Groves
cards.flavor: Whoever plants an olive tree plants it for strangers: it takes a lifetime to bear, then gives oil for centuries.

cards.name: House of Life
cards.flavor: In Egypt's House of Life, scribes copy sacred texts by lamplight, and physicians learn their spells and cures side by side.

cards.name: Qanat
cards.flavor: Diggers tunnel into the hillside after water no one has seen, and lead it for miles through the dark to the desert fields.

cards.name: Fishing Huts
cards.flavor: Reed huts on the shore, nets drying in the sun, and the boats out at dawn on water the colour of pewter.

cards.name: Salt Pans
cards.flavor: Seawater stands in shallow clay beds until the sun takes the water and leaves the salt, and the catch keeps till winter.

cards.name: Shrine
cards.flavor: A small altar on a high place. Travellers leave a bead or a crust for the mountain spirit, just in case, and do not look back.

cards.name: Mine
cards.flavor: Miners follow the green-streaked rock into the hill with fire and antler picks, for copper, tin and silver, and come out blinking.

cards.name: Shaft Mine
cards.flavor: Shafts and galleries reach deep under the hill, where the lamps burn low and the richest ore is always a little deeper.

cards.name: Forge
cards.flavor: In the forge the bellows roar and ore becomes bronze, then iron: blades, ploughshares, and the power to keep a land.

cards.name: Barracks
cards.flavor: The young are drilled to march in step and hold the line, until one morning the city finds it has an army, and wonders what for.

cards.name: Market
cards.flavor: In the market square everything is for sale, and everything has been sold before: the pots, the figs, the news.

cards.name: Granary
cards.flavor: The surplus of the good years is sealed in clay bins against the lean ones. The lean years always come; only the date is unknown.

cards.name: Chiefdom
cards.flavor: The chief is whoever the elders can agree on, which means the one with the most cattle and the longest memory for favours.

quote.text: They choose their kings by birth, their generals for merit.

cards.name: Kingship
cards.flavor: One ruler, one palace, one treasury, one throne, and a line of heirs, each of whom has quietly measured the throne.

quote.text: When kingship was lowered from heaven, the kingship was in Eridu.

cards.name: Theocracy
cards.flavor: In the god's city the priests keep the land, the granaries and the calendar, and every law is a prayer someone has answered.

quote.text: Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.

cards.name: Anarchy
cards.flavor: When the old order breaks, no one rules and everyone does. Debts are burned, granaries thrown open, and each day the loudest voice decides.

quote.text: Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold; mere anarchy is loosed upon the world.
quote.by: W. B. Yeats, The Second Coming

cards.text: 1 action each turn. Only order cards can be played; nothing can be grown, bought or researched. Each turn it eats 20% of stored food and wealth. Lasts up to 4 turns, fewer the calmer the people; calming shortens it. From its second turn, buy order for 2, 6, 12 or 20 wealth with 1–4 turns left. When it ends, choose a government from your government deck. Each turn: trash 1 card, +1 per turn so far, from your hand, deck or discard (−1 unrest each).

cards.name: Egypt
cards.flavor: Along the thin green ribbon of the Nile the yearly flood lays down its black silt, and the pharaohs raise monuments meant to outlast time. Some of them do.

quote.text: Egypt is the gift of the river.

cards.name: Sumer
cards.flavor: Between the Tigris and the Euphrates the Sumerians dig canals, build the first cities, and press wedges into clay to keep their accounts. Writing begins as a receipt.

quote.text: Go up on the wall of Uruk and walk around.

cards.name: Phoenicia
cards.flavor: From Tyre and Sidon, Phoenician ships carry cedar, glass and purple dye across the Mediterranean, and leave their alphabet in every port they touch.

quote.text: A merchant of the people for many isles.

cards.name: Babylon
cards.flavor: Hammurabi carves his laws in stone for all to see, and Babylon's astronomers keep the most careful records of the heavens in the ancient world, night after night.

quote.text: That the strong should not harm the weak.

cards.name: Greece
cards.flavor: Rival city-states argue in the agora, stage tragedies in open theatres, and ask the questions philosophers are still asking, with no better answers.

quote.text: The unexamined life is not worth living.

cards.name: Persia
cards.flavor: Cyrus and Darius rule the largest empire yet seen, held together by satraps, respect for local custom, and a road of relay stations from Sardis to Susa.

quote.text: Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night stays these couriers from the swift completion of their appointed rounds.

cards.name: Harvest Festival
cards.flavor: The last sheaf comes home with songs, and for one night the village eats as if winter were only a story.

cards.name: Scribal School
cards.flavor: In the tablet house, children copy signs into wet clay for years, until they can keep the temple's accounts in their sleep.

cards.name: Library
cards.flavor: Tablets and rolls of law, medicine and the stars line the shelves, and somewhere among them is an answer no one has asked for.

cards.name: Stone Circle
cards.flavor: The ring of great stones is a calendar no one can carry: the seasons must come to it, and every midsummer they do.

cards.name: Courtyard Houses
cards.flavor: Rooms open onto a shaded courtyard where the family cooks, quarrels and works, and on summer nights sleeps under the stars.

cards.name: Bathhouse
cards.flavor: Warm pools, cold plunges and gossip: the bathhouse keeps the city clean, and settles more business than the courthouse.

cards.name: Courthouse
cards.flavor: Judges hear disputes by the written law, so that the strong may not simply take from the weak, at least not in public.

cards.name: Aqueduct
cards.flavor: Stone channels carry clean water from the distant hills across the valleys on great arches: a river on stilts, walking into town.

cards.name: Palace
cards.flavor: The ruler's household, treasury and court gather under one roof, and from its painted halls the realm is governed, mostly in whispers.

cards.name: Shipyard
cards.flavor: Shipwrights shape cedar and pine into hulls that smell of resin, and every vessel launched carries the city a little further out.

cards.name: Terraced Fields
cards.flavor: Stone walls step up the slope, each holding a strip of soil where no field could lie: a staircase built for the harvest.

cards.name: Reed Works
cards.flavor: Marsh reeds are cut and bundled for boats, mats, baskets and houses, and for the scribe's pen, so the swamp writes its own history.

cards.name: Cistern
cards.flavor: Plastered chambers in the rock catch every winter rain and keep it cool and sweet through the long dry summer, like a secret.

cards.name: Dye Works
cards.flavor: Thousands of sea snails make one pinch of Tyrian purple, worth more than its weight in silver. The vats stink for miles.

cards.name: Kiln
cards.flavor: Potters fire the riverbank's mud into jars, lamps and bricks, and their kilns glow all night along the water like small sunsets.

cards.name: Merchant Quarter
cards.flavor: Warehouses, counting houses and foreign traders fill one district, where fortunes turn and everyone dresses slightly above their means.

cards.name: Mint
cards.flavor: Lydia strikes the first coins of electrum, stamped with a lion, and soon every city wants its own, as neighbours always do.

cards.name: Storehouse
cards.flavor: Rows of storerooms hold grain, oil and wine, tallied by seal and tablet against famine and siege, and against forgetting.

cards.name: City Walls
cards.flavor: Stone walls, towers and gates ring the city. Inside, a siege is now counted in months; outside, in patience.

cards.name: Multi-storey Houses
cards.flavor: As the city fills, houses rise two and three storeys, shops below and families above, and every wall is thin enough to hear through.

cards.name: Textile Works
cards.flavor: Hundreds of workers spin, weave and dye under one master, and the cloth leaves by the cartload for markets they will never see.

cards.name: Dockyard
cards.flavor: Slipways, ropewalks and timber stores line the waterfront, and ships come off them faster than any rival can launch its own.

cards.name: Caravan Station
cards.flavor: A walled courtyard a day's march from the last, where camels drink at the well and merchants trade news by lamplight.

cards.name: Envoys from the Hills
cards.flavor: Hill chieftains arrive with furs, honey and great courtesy. Everyone understands that the gifts are a kind of bill.

cards.name: Plague
cards.flavor: A fever comes up the river with the boats. The healers burn herbs, the streets go quiet, and the gravediggers do not rest.

cards.name: Granary Fire
cards.flavor: A lamp tips over in the night, and by dawn a season's grain is ash and smoke.

cards.name: Drought
cards.flavor: No rain since the spring sowing. The plains crack, and each day the herds walk farther to drink.

cards.name: Silt Flood
cards.flavor: The river rises over its banks and, going, leaves behind a gift of black mud, thick and rich.

cards.name: Bumper Harvest
cards.flavor: The ears hang so heavy the stalks bend, and every barn is full to the rafters. Everyone says they knew it would be a good year.

cards.name: Busy Harbours
cards.flavor: Sails crowd every bay, and the quays ring with a dozen languages, all of them haggling.

cards.name: Visiting Scholar
cards.flavor: A stranger who reads the stars and counts in strange numerals asks only for a roof, a lamp, and no questions.

cards.name: Labour Shortage
cards.flavor: The young have gone to the mines and the boats, and the fields wait for hands that do not come.

cards.name: Tax Revolt
cards.flavor: The tax collectors come back empty-handed and bloodied. The villages say they have paid enough, and this time they say it together.

cards.name: Wandering Smiths
cards.flavor: Smiths from the far hills set up a forge by the gate and offer their secrets, for a price, with the charm of people who never stay.

cards.name: Pestilence
cards.flavor: The sickness spreads through the crowded streets faster than the priests can name it.

cards.name: Library Burns
cards.flavor: The scrolls catch like dry grass, and a hundred years of learning rises into the night sky.

cards.name: Debased Coin
cards.flavor: The mint cuts the silver with lead. Soon the merchants weigh every coin twice and trust none of them.

cards.name: Storm at Sea
cards.flavor: Three days of gales, and the harbours fill with wreckage instead of cargo.

cards.name: Golden Age
cards.flavor: Peace, full granaries and clever hands: for a few bright years everything the realm attempts succeeds, and no one asks for how long.

cards.name: School of Philosophers
cards.flavor: Under the plane trees, teachers argue about the nature of things until the shadows reach them, and their students write it all down.

cards.name: Succession Crisis
cards.flavor: The old ruler dies with three heirs and no will. Each heir has friends with swords, and all of them are in mourning.

cards.name: Mercenaries' Offer
cards.flavor: Hard people with foreign shields wait at the gate, courteous and patient. They will fight for anyone who pays in silver.

cards.name: Solstice Rites
cards.flavor: On the longest night, fires burn on every hill, and the elders watch the east for the sun to turn back.

cards.name: Traveling Bards
cards.flavor: Strangers with lyres trade songs of far-off kings for a meal and a place by the fire, and the kings grow grander with every cup.

cards.name: Comet Sighted
cards.flavor: A long-haired star hangs over the fields for weeks. The priests argue whether it foretells a birth or a death, and predict both.

cards.name: Distant Drums
cards.flavor: From beyond the hills, drums beat through the night. No one has seen the drummers yet. No one goes to look.

cards.name: Wild Berries
cards.flavor: The hedges hang heavy with fruit, and the children come home in the long gold evenings with purple hands and purple mouths.

cards.name: Tuna Run
cards.flavor: In early summer the tuna run along the coast in shoals so thick the water seems to boil, and every boat goes out.

cards.name: Beached Whale
cards.flavor: A whale lies stranded on the sand at dawn. By noon the whole town is there with knives and baskets, and nobody asks whose it is.

cards.name: Shipwreck Salvage
cards.flavor: A foreign ship breaks up on the reef in the night. By morning its amphorae, timber and rope lie along the shore.

cards.name: Wandering Trader
cards.flavor: A lone trader leads a laden donkey into the square, with salt, beads and news from the coast, and a special price just for you.

cards.name: Local Legend
cards.flavor: A shepherd wrestles a lion and becomes a hero. By the third retelling, it was two lions.

cards.name: Mild Spring
cards.flavor: The thaw comes early and gentle, the rivers rise just enough, and people go about their days as if they had been forgiven.

cards.name: Famine
cards.flavor: The granaries echo. Families eat the seed grain, then the oxen, and wait for the next harvest.
cards.text: Each hungry upkeep: +1 counter (max 3), −1 pop (largest territory) and +1 unrest per counter. Ends when your pop is fed.

cards.name: Market Day
cards.flavor: The square fills with stalls, haggling and gossip, and coins change hands faster than rumours, though not by much.

cards.name: Good Omens
cards.flavor: An eagle circles the citadel three times, and the augurs declare the gods well pleased, and take the afternoon off.

cards.name: Grumbling
cards.flavor: At the wells and in the taverns, people mutter about taxes, the harvest and their rulers, in voices not quite low enough.

cards.name: Omen of Doom
cards.flavor: A calf is born with two heads and the moon rises red. The soothsayers, so talkative all spring, will not meet anyone's eye.

cards.name: Bandit Raids
cards.flavor: Masked riders work the roads at dusk, and caravans arrive late, or light, or not at all.

cards.name: Raiders
cards.flavor: Dust on the horizon: riders from the steppe, come for the harvest.

cards.name: Sea Raiders
cards.flavor: Long ships are beached in the night, and by morning the harbour stores are gone, and so are they.

cards.name: Hill Tribes
cards.flavor: The clans of the high valleys come down when their own stores run thin, the way poor relations do.

cards.name: Calls for Reform
cards.flavor: Petitioners crowd the palace steps, asking for fairer laws and a say in making them. The palace minds the second part more.

cards.name: Peasant Uprising
cards.flavor: Pitchforks and torches: the farmers have had enough, and the steward's house burns first.

cards.name: Radical Thinkers
cards.flavor: In the agora, teachers question the gods, the laws and the king, quietly and reasonably, and the young listen as they never do at home.

cards.name: Pottery
cards.flavor: Fired clay holds grain, water and oil through the seasons, and when it breaks, the sherds stay behind to say who lived there.

quote.text: Who is the Potter, pray, and who the Pot?
quote.by: Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám, tr. Edward FitzGerald

cards.name: Animal Husbandry
cards.flavor: Wild aurochs, goats and sheep become herds: milk, wool, hides, and patient strength for the plough.

quote.text: The master's eye fattens the horse.

cards.name: Irrigation
cards.flavor: Canals and ditches lead the river out to thirsty fields, and the desert's edge turns green, a few paces every year.

quote.text: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

cards.name: The Plough
cards.flavor: Yoked oxen drag a wooden share through heavy soil, and one family sows what once took a village. The village must find other work.

quote.text: We must cultivate our garden.

cards.name: Weaving
cards.flavor: Flax and wool, spun and woven on upright looms, become cloth, the greatest trade of the ancient world after bread.

quote.text: Oh, what a tangled web we weave, when first we practise to deceive!

cards.name: Clay Tokens
cards.flavor: Little clay cones, spheres and discs stand for sheep and measures of grain, sealed in a clay envelope as a receipt.

quote.text: God made the integers; all else is the work of man.

cards.name: Fermentation
cards.flavor: Grain left wet in a jar turns to beer, which keeps for months. Sumerian workers draw their wages in it, and seldom complain.

quote.text: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man.

cards.name: Mining
cards.flavor: Copper, tin and flint are dug from the hills through narrow shafts, lit by oil lamps that are never bright enough.

quote.text: All that glisters is not gold.
quote.by: William Shakespeare, The Merchant of Venice

cards.name: Mysticism
cards.flavor: Shamans and seers read meaning in stars, dreams and entrails, and the first shrines rise to hold what cannot be explained.

quote.text: There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, than are dreamt of in your philosophy.

cards.name: The Wheel
cards.flavor: First turned by potters in Mesopotamia, the wheel soon carries carts, chariots and trade across the plains, and never stops.

quote.text: There is no new thing under the sun.

cards.name: Masonry
cards.flavor: Cut stone, fitted so close a blade will not pass, raises walls, tombs and temples meant to stand forever. Some nearly do.

quote.text: I found Rome a city of bricks and left it a city of marble.
quote.by: Augustus, in Suetonius' Lives of the Caesars

cards.name: Bronze Working
cards.flavor: Copper alloyed with tin makes harder blades and tools, and a hunger for tin that sends traders across unknown seas.

quote.text: I have raised a monument more lasting than bronze.

cards.name: Writing
cards.flavor: Marks pressed into clay to count grain grow into laws, letters and epics: a way of keeping the harvest becomes a way of keeping the dead.

quote.text: The written word remains.

cards.name: Weights and Measures
cards.flavor: Silver weighed out in shekels and grain in fixed measures let strangers trade without haggling over every sack. Mostly.

quote.text: Man is the measure of all things.

cards.name: Olive and Vine
cards.flavor: Olive trees and vines take years to bear, then bear for lifetimes, and their oil and wine sail out in amphorae.

quote.text: They shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid.

cards.name: Medicine
cards.flavor: In Egypt's Houses of Life, priest-physicians copy papyri on wounds, fevers and remedies, and tend the sick by lamplight.

quote.text: Life is short, the art long.

cards.name: Credit
cards.flavor: Temple and palace lend silver and barley at interest on clay contracts. Debtors who cannot repay are sold; the contracts are kept.

quote.text: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

cards.name: Sailing
cards.flavor: Reed boats, then planked hulls under square sails, carry cargo, colonists and ideas along the coasts, and bring strangers home.

quote.text: To sail is necessary; to live is not.
quote.by: Pompey, in Plutarch's Life of Pompey

cards.name: Priesthood
cards.flavor: A class of priests keeps the temples, the rites and the granaries, and speaks to kings for the gods, in a tone kings dislike.

quote.text: Many are called, but few are chosen.

cards.name: Code of Laws
cards.flavor: Written laws, set in stone for all to read, replace the chief's whim with fixed rules. The chief takes it personally.

quote.text: Let the good of the people be the supreme law.

cards.name: Calendar
cards.flavor: Watching the Nile's flood and the rising of Sirius, the Egyptians count a year of 365 days, and the stars drift a quarter day a year.

quote.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven.

cards.name: Philosophy
cards.flavor: Greek thinkers ask what the world is made of and how one should live, and answer with reason rather than myth, which is harder.

quote.text: Philosophy begins in wonder.

cards.name: Iron Working
cards.flavor: Iron is harder to smelt than bronze, but its ore is everywhere: soon every farmer has an iron blade, and opinions.

quote.text: For now truly is a race of iron, and men never rest from labour and sorrow by day.

cards.name: Mathematics
cards.flavor: Babylonian tables, Egyptian surveyors and Greek geometers turn counting into proof, true whatever anyone believes.

quote.text: There is no royal road to geometry.
quote.by: Euclid to Ptolemy I, in Proclus

cards.name: Coinage
cards.flavor: Lydian kings stamp lumps of electrum with a lion's head, and a coin's worth no longer needs a balance, only faith in the lion.

quote.text: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.

cards.name: Bureaucracy
cards.flavor: Satraps govern the provinces, scribes keep the tax rolls, and royal couriers ride between them with orders already out of date.

quote.text: Who will guard the guards themselves?

cards.name: Alphabet
cards.flavor: Phoenician traders cut hundreds of signs down to 22 letters, and reading is no longer for scribes alone.

quote.text: In the beginning was the Word.

cards.name: Qanat
cards.flavor: Persian diggers tunnel gently downhill from a mountain's water table, and in the middle of the desert, impossibly, a field.

quote.text: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.

cards.name: Navigation
cards.flavor: Steering by the stars, Phoenician ships leave the coast behind and cross open sea to Carthage and Gades, where the known world ends.

quote.text: When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.

cards.name: Astronomy
cards.flavor: Atop the ziggurats, priests chart the wandering stars, learn to foretell eclipses, and tell the king only what he needs to know.

quote.text: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.

cards.name: Engineering
cards.flavor: Arches, aqueducts and roads carry water and armies across whole provinces, in straight lines that ignore the hills.

quote.text: Give me a place to stand, and I will move the earth.
